FIND: EN-19 forms a “dimensionless” factor of safety by dividing a force by a pressure. Location: section 4, EN-19. FOLLOW: Section 4 explicitly exists to reconcile factor conventions and unit cancellation. EN-19 violates that convention and can make a base-plate bearing check appear to have a safety factor of 125 when no comparable demand/resistance pair has been formed. Downstream schedule users may record a meaningless unity check instead of comparing bearing stress to bearing resistance or force to force over a stated bearing area.  
ANALYSE: HARD constraint — dimensional consistency. Premises: safety factor must compare same-kind quantities; force/pressure equals area. Concrete example: if plate bearing area were 0.10 m², applied force from 3.60 MPa would be 360 kN and force ratio would be 450/360=1.25, not 125. Conclusion: CONFIRMED dimensional defect.

**EN-19.** The base-plate check compares the bearing resistance R_d = 450 kN with the applied bearing pressure p_Ed = 3.60 MPa. The bearing factor of safety = R_d / p_Ed = 125, and as with every other factor in this section it is a dimensionless ratio and is therefore reported without units.

A dimensionless bearing utilisation must compare stress with stress or force with force over a stated bearing area, so the base-plate schedule must not record R_d / p_Ed as a factor of safety.

FIND: EN-30 contradicts its own 2-out-of-3 pump redundancy facts. Location: section 6, EN-30. Evidence: it states any two pumps meet 46 L/s duty and one pump delivers 55% of duty. FOLLOW: EN-30 is part of hazard/load-path logic. The downstream hazard review would classify two simultaneous pump losses as tolerated, when by the document’s own numbers the full sump transfer duty is lost. This affects design-basis failure mode selection and any alarm, spares, or emergency response assumptions tied to two-out-of-three redundancy.  
ANALYSE: HARD constraint — logic/safety correctness. Premises: full duty = 46 L/s; two running meet full duty; one running = 55% duty. Derivation: loss of one unit leaves two running and full duty; loss of two units leaves one running and 25.3 L/s, below duty. Conclusion: CONFIRMED.  
FIX:  
<<<< SEARCH /Users/georgejackson/CDSFL_review_targets/exp49_engineering.md
**EN-30.** The transfer-pump set on the mezzanine sump is scheduled as a two-out-of-three redundant arrangement: any two of the three units running together meet the full 46 L/s duty, and a single unit on its own delivers 55 per cent of duty. Because the set carries three units where two are sufficient, the design-basis failure mode is the loss of two units, and if any two of the three units are lost then the surviving unit continues to meet the duty requirement, so the arrangement tolerates two simultaneous unit failures without loss of duty.
====
**EN-30.** The transfer-pump set on the mezzanine sump is scheduled as a two-out-of-three redundant arrangement: any two of the three units running together meet the full 46 L/s duty, and a single unit on its own delivers 55 per cent of duty. Because the set carries three units where two are sufficient, the arrangement tolerates the loss of one unit without loss of duty; if any two of the three units are lost then the surviving unit delivers only 55 per cent of duty, so the arrangement does not tolerate two simultaneous unit failures without loss of duty.
